background.text: You had talked about the negativity of the ads. And I think we've all seen negative ads all of our life. But it seems like this year it is really ratcheted up.

I would think if you're such a great candidate, if you're such a fine and qualified candidate to be the governor or to be the president or be that state senator, you would have so many plans and so many agendas that you want to talk about and so many issues you want to talk about with your constituents that you would spend 95% of your time talking about your plans, talking about what you intend to do. But we don't see that a lot. What we see a lot of is people trying to smirch other people's character to knock somebody else down, to ratchet themselves up. I think the people of this state and, quite frankly, the nation, they're starting to see through that. They're starting to see right through the heart of the matter. And they're starting to ask the essential question, what have you really done? What are you willing to do? What have you laid out as your plan to help the people? And when they don't see any substance there, oftentimes those negative ads don't want them.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: What is the one thing, if you were elected governor, what's the one policy or whatever that you really want to do, make sure that you get accomplished?

ground_truth: Well, you know, I wouldn't say it's one thing in particular. We talked about those five pillars of our economy, and we talked about building an economy through those five pillars and how the governor plays a role in that. But the ultimate goal here for me is this. One of the things, well, actually the thing that distressed me the most is when I was running for lieutenant governor and I traveled to all 100 counties in this state, the disparaging of economic opportunity in this state from one point in the state to the other. You go through Grainsboro and Charlotte and High Point and Winston and Rollitt, you know, and you see great economic opportunity everywhere you turn. But you head east and you head west, and all of a sudden you see what some people say is a lack of opportunity. What I see when I travel this state to the east and western part of the states is not lack of opportunity. I see opportunities not taken advantage of. It's time for this state to stand up and start taking advantage of those opportunities. So the ultimate goal here through working through the governor's mansion and working with the legislature to continue to build our economy is a dream that I have to build an economy in this state that spans from Murphy to Mania. And as you drive across this state, you don't see any more of those economically depressed places. You see vibrant places where people are making a great living right where they live, no matter what their zip code is. And that is the ultimate goal. And for me, being governor, I know I couldn't do that in four years or even eight years. But many, many years from now, if I'm an old man and I look back and I say, hey, I was part of the team to start the process that made this state even greater and built this great economy that spans from Murphy to Mania, I think that probably would be my proudest accomplishment.
